claims.head: The Golden Knights’ defense joins the attack, the Wild’s stays home
claims.body: The Golden Knights’ defensemen shoot a lot, and the Wild’s not so much. Vegas is near the top of the league for shots from defensemen, and Minnesota is one of the worst. Watch the Golden Knights’ defensemen jump into the play.

notes.text: Rasmus Andersson is no longer killing penalties: 3% of the team’s shorthanded time in 6 games, down from 48% last season.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 5 games cover only 33% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the third-lowest in the league (a typical team: 47%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

MIN.head: A tough matchup for the Wild
MIN.body: Even though Minnesota has home-ice advantage, Vegas has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Wild’s best way through is keeping dangerous shots away.

VGK.head: Advantage, the Golden Knights
VGK.body: Even though Minnesota has home-ice advantage, Vegas has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Wild can make it interesting if they keep dangerous shots away.

story.head: Best against best
paras: The Wild are 3-1-1. The Golden Knights have won four straight. Two of the league’s best teams meet.
The Golden Knights’ power play has a soft target in the Wild’s kill. The Knights’ defensemen shoot a lot, and the Wild’s not so much.

items.text: The Wild are newly without Marcus Foligno, and have had to make do without Filip Gustavsson and Brock Faber all season. Jesper Wallstedt is expected to start.
The Golden Knights are newly without Victor Olofsson.
Mark Stone has a point in five straight games against Minnesota.
Jack Eichel is one assist from passing Jonathan Marchessault for fourth on the Golden Knights’ all-time assists list.
